legend.evaluated: Looked at seriously; kept as an alternative
legend.rejected: Looked at and set aside, with the reason

items.name: Python 3.12 via uv
items.plain: The language everything is written in, on a modern version. uv installs it without needing Homebrew.
items.why: System Python 3.9 is end-of-life and current vision libraries target 3.10+.

items.name: PyTorch on Apple MPS
items.plain: The engine that runs the neural networks, using the Mac's GPU.
items.why: Only accelerator on the machine; a device setting swaps to CUDA on a rented box.

items.name: Apple M4, 16 GB
items.plain: The laptop. No cloud GPU yet.
items.why: Free, and enough for a small real-time detector on 1080p film.

items.name: NFL API (api.nfl.com)
items.plain: The NFL's own feed: every play, down, distance, yard line, and which jersey numbers touched the ball.
items.why: Official, per-play ids, and it names players per play, which trains identity for free.

items.name: nflverse (nfl_data_py)
items.plain: Free public play-by-play with formation and personnel labels for past seasons.
items.why: The NFL API does not carry personnel or formation; nflverse does.

items.name: Big Data Bowl tracking data
items.plain: Kaggle's NFL player-tracking datasets, same shape as what our vision layer will produce.
items.why: Lets the football-intelligence code be validated before the vision code is trustworthy.

items.name: DuckDB + Parquet
items.plain: Files on disk that act like a fast database.
items.why: Columnar, joins a season in memory on 16 GB, no server to run.

items.name: PyAV (bundled ffmpeg)
items.plain: Reads and writes video files frame by frame.
items.why: Already used for shot detection; frame-accurate seeking; no system install.

items.name: OpenCV
items.plain: Image maths: warping, line finding, drawing.
items.why: The standard toolbox for homography and drawing.

items.name: SAM 3 (Meta)
items.plain: A big model you can point at a picture and say 'football player' and it finds them all. Used to make our training data, and on the few frames sent for deep reasoning.
items.why: Best open model for finding things by name. Too slow on a laptop to run on every frame, so it teaches the fast model instead.

items.name: SAM 3D Body (Meta)
items.plain: Turns one photo of a person into a 3D skeleton.
items.why: This is what lets the 3D replay show real body poses rather than capsules.

items.name: RF-DETR (Roboflow)
items.plain: The fast detector that runs on every frame once trained.
items.why: Apache-licensed, real-time, accurate, safe to distribute.

items.name: YOLO11 / YOLO26 (Ultralytics)
items.plain: The quickest path to a first detector.
items.why: Great for a prototype; AGPL license means it cannot ship in a distributed product without care.

items.name: ByteTrack (via supervision)
items.plain: Follows each detected player from frame to frame and gives them a stable id.
items.why: Cheap and robust; association is on boxes only.

items.name: SigLIP team classifier
items.plain: Sorts player crops into home, away, and officials by how they look.
items.why: Borrowed from roboflow/sports; no labels needed.

items.name: YOLO11-pose / RTMPose
items.plain: 2D body keypoints on every frame: stance, contact, height.
items.why: Fast enough for every frame; SAM 3D Body is reserved for keyframes.

items.name: EasyOCR
items.plain: Reads text (jersey numbers) from image crops.
items.why: Offline fallback for jersey reads; runs on Apple Silicon.

items.name: PaddleOCR
items.plain: Another text reader.
items.why: PaddlePaddle wheels are unreliable on Apple Silicon.

items.name: SAM 2 (Meta)
items.plain: The previous segmentation model.
items.why: Lighter than SAM 3; kept as the fallback if SAM 3 weights are gated.

items.name: Claude (Anthropic) via the official SDK
items.plain: The hosted model that answers chat questions today, and later looks at hard frames (piles, contested catches).
items.why: Already in the repo; structured outputs; one vendor relationship. The only hosted piece of the system.

items.name: OpenAI / Gemini providers
items.plain: Alternative hosted vision models behind the same interface.
items.why: Keeps the vendor swappable with a config change.

items.name: Pydantic v2 + pydantic-settings
items.plain: Checks that every data record and every model response has the right shape.
items.why: Validates provider responses and Parquet schemas; config lives in YAML, not code.

items.name: pytest, ruff
items.plain: Tests and linting.
items.why: 158 tests pass today.

items.name: Custom review sheets (HTML)
items.plain: A web page with keyboard shortcuts for approving auto-generated labels.
items.why: No CVAT or Roboflow account needed; decisions save to a JSON file that gets versioned.

items.name: This tracker (docs + build.py + Render)
items.plain: Markdown and JSON in the repo, compiled to a static site.
items.why: One source of truth, no database, auto-deploys on push.
